messages.author: 4d7ad7ef3cf75f92
messages.subject: problem with variables within ggplot() function
parts:
Hello.
I can not use ggplot() function in loop:

Example:

I have data frame A with variables X1,X2,X3,Factor_1,Factor_2,Factor_3
where
X1,...,X3 are continous variables;
Factor_1,...,Factor_3 are categorial variables

I have vector MyVec = c("Factor_1","Factor_2","Factor_3")

I would like to plot kernel densities for all variables X1,X2,X3 with
loop, but I can not do this in that way:

# ---
pdf("C:/example.pdf")

for (i in 1:3){
for (k in 1:3) {
my.plot = ggplot(A, aes(x=colnames(A)[i], colour=MyVec[k],
group=MyVec[k]))
my.kde.ggplot = my.plot +
geom_density(fill=NA)
print(my.kde.ggplot)

}
}

dev.off()

# ---

How can I create plots within loop when arguments in ggplot() function
do change?

messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Re: problem with variables within ggplot() function
parts:
Hi jyk -

It's very hard to tell what you want to do.  Generally speaking you should always make use of the scoping rules used by ggplot2 - never refer to variable names in the way that you do (e.g. colnames(A)[i]).  Refer to them directly as X1, X2, or X3.  If you need to do it for a bunch of them, melt the data.frame.  Maybe these examples provide a basis to launch from?

library(ggplot2)

df <- data.frame(
  x = rnorm(30),
  y = rnorm(30),
  z = rnorm(30),
  a = sample(paste('a', 1:3, sep = ''), 10, replace = TRUE),
  b = sample(paste('b', 1:3, sep = ''), 10, replace = TRUE),
  c = sample(paste('c', 1:3, sep = ''), 10, replace = TRUE)
)
mdf <- melt(df, id.vars = c('a','b','c'))

qplot(value, data = mdf, geom = 'density', colour = variable, facets = a ~ .)

mdf <- melt(mdf, id.vars = c('variable','value')) # better way to do this from df?
names(mdf) <- c('contvar', 'value', 'catvar', 'cohort')

qplot(value, data = mdf, geom = 'density', colour = cohort, 
  facets = catvar ~ contvar)

Hope it helps
david.

Another option would be to use aes_string() instead of aes() to define your variables, then it should work. Here is an example (without data). 

require(ggplot2)


df.data<-read.delim("/Users/bhurr/Desktop/bw_export_data.txt")


colstart=3

colend=6

colend <- ncol(df.data)


for (i in colstart:colend){

plot<-ggplot()+

geom_boxplot(data=df.data, aes_string(x= paste(colnames(df.data)[2]), y= paste(colnames(df.data)[i])))+

theme_bw()

 

#save plot

ggsave(sprintf("Boxplot.%s.png", colnames(df.data)[i]), width=6, height=6)

}


HTH, 


Brandon
